statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When an SMTP client has a message to transmit, it establishes a two-way transmission channel to an SMTP server.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Once the transmission channel is established and initial handshaking is completed, the SMTP client normally initiates a mail transaction.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Such a transaction consists of a series of commands to specify the originator and destination of the mail and transmission of the message content (including any lines in the header section or other structure) itself.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: When an SMTP client has a message to transmit, it establishes a two-way transmission channel to an SMTP server.
actions: establish two-way transmission channel to SMTP server

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Once the transmission channel is established and initial handshaking is completed, the SMTP client normally initiates a mail transaction.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: once the server has issued a success response at the end of the mail data, a formal handoff of responsibility for the message occurs: the protocol requires that a server MUST accept responsibility for either delivering the message or properly reporting the failure to do so
statements.trigger: server issues success response at end of mail data
actions: formal handoff of responsibility for message to server

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once a given mail message has been transmitted, the client may either request that the connection be shut down or may initiate other mail transactions.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once a given mail message has been transmitted, the client may either request that the connection be shut down or may initiate other mail transactions.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If an intermediate SMTP system finds a next hop that does not support the required extension, it MAY choose, based on the specific extension and circumstances, to requeue the message and try later and/or try an alternate MX host.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If this strategy is employed, the timeout to fall back to an unextended format (if one is available) SHOULD be less than the normal timeout for bouncing as undeliverable.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The domain name given in the EHLO command MUST be either a primary host name (a domain name that resolves to an address RR) or, if the host has no name, an address literal, as described in Section 4.1.3 and discussed further in the EHLO discussion of Section 4.1.4.
allowed_values: primary host name (FQDN resolving to address RR)
statements.guard_semantics: EHLO domain must be FQDN resolving to address RR or address literal if host has no name

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Only resolvable, fully-qualified domain names (FQDNs) are permitted when domain names are used in SMTP. Local nicknames or unqualified names MUST NOT be used. Local aliases MUST NOT appear in any SMTP transaction.
allowed_values: CNAME resolving to MX or address RR
statements.guard_semantics: domain.is_fqdn = true & domain.is_resolvable = true

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The reserved mailbox name 'postmaster' may be used in a RCPT command without domain qualification and MUST be accepted if so used.
actions: accept RCPT TO postmaster without domain qualification

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SMTP sessions are stateful, with both parties carefully maintaining a common view of the current state. This state is modeled by a virtual 'buffer' and a 'state table' on the server.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SMTP sessions are stateful, with both parties carefully maintaining a common view of the current state. This state is modeled by a virtual 'buffer' and a 'state table' on the server.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The client may 'clear the buffer' or 'reset the state table', causing the information in the buffer to be discarded and the state to be returned to some previous state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An SMTP reply is an acknowledgment (positive or negative) sent in lines from receiver to sender via the transmission channel in response to a command.
actions: send reply with numeric completion code

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The general form of a reply is a numeric completion code (indicating failure or success) usually followed by a text string.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An SMTP session is initiated when a client opens a connection to a server and the server responds with an opening message.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The SMTP protocol allows a server to formally reject a mail session while still allowing the initial connection: a 554 response MAY be given in the initial connection opening message instead of the 220. A server taking this approach MUST still wait for the client to send a QUIT before closing the connection and SHOULD respond to any intervening commands with '503 bad sequence of commands'.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A 554 response MAY be given in the initial connection opening message instead of the 220.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An SMTP session is initiated when a client opens a connection to a server and the server responds with an opening message (220).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A 554 response MAY be given in the initial connection opening message instead of the 220 to formally reject a mail session.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A server taking this approach MUST still wait for the client to send a QUIT before closing the connection.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A server SHOULD respond to any intervening commands with '503 bad sequence of commands' after sending 554 on connection opening.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once the server has sent the greeting (welcoming) message and the client has received it, the client normally sends the EHLO command to the server, indicating the client's identity. In addition to opening the session, use of EHLO indicates that the client is able to process service extensions and requests that the server provide a list of the extensions it supports.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Older SMTP systems that are unable to support service extensions, and contemporary clients that do not require service extensions in the mail session being initiated, MAY use HELO instead of EHLO.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: For a particular connection attempt, if the server returns a 'command not recognized' response to EHLO, the client SHOULD be able to fall back and send HELO.
statements.trigger: server returns command-not-recognized response to EHLO

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MUST NOT return the extended EHLO-style response to a HELO command.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: the MAIL command may be sent only when no mail transaction is in progress

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: This command tells the SMTP-receiver that a new mail transaction is starting and to reset all its state tables and buffers, including any recipients or mail data.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If accepted, the SMTP server returns a 354 Intermediate reply and considers all succeeding lines up to but not including the end of mail data indicator to be the message text.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The transaction starts with a MAIL command that gives the sender identification. This command tells the SMTP-receiver that a new mail transaction is starting and to reset all its state tables and buffers. If accepted, the SMTP server returns a 250 OK reply.
actions: reset all state tables and buffers including recipients and mail data

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A series of one or more RCPT commands follows, giving the receiver information. If accepted, the SMTP server returns a 250 OK reply and stores the forward-path. This step of the procedure can be repeated any number of times.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A DATA command initiates transfer of the mail data. If accepted, the SMTP server returns a 354 Intermediate reply and considers all succeeding lines up to but not including the end of mail data indicator to be the message text.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When the end of text is successfully received and stored, the SMTP-receiver sends a 250 OK reply. The end of mail data indicator also confirms the mail transaction and tells the SMTP server to now process the stored recipients and mail data.
statements.trigger: end of mail data received and accepted
actions: process stored recipients and mail data

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a RCPT command appears without a previous MAIL command, the server MUST return a 503 'Bad sequence of commands' response.
statements.trigger: RCPT command received without prior MAIL

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If there was no MAIL, or no RCPT, command, or all such commands were rejected, the server MAY return a 'command out of sequence' (503) or 'no valid recipients' (554) reply in response to the DATA command.
statements.trigger: DATA command with no MAIL or no valid RCPT

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If one of those replies (or any other 5yz reply) is received, the client MUST NOT send the message data; more generally, message data MUST NOT be sent unless a 354 reply is received.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Mail transaction commands MUST be used in the order discussed above.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MAY forward messages when they are aware of an address change. When they do so, they MAY either provide address-updating information with a 251 code, or may forward 'silently' and return a 250 code.
statements.trigger: RCPT received with known address change

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MAY reject messages or return them as non-deliverable when they cannot be delivered precisely as addressed. When they do so, they MAY either provide address-updating information with a 551 code, or may reject the message as undeliverable with a 550 code and no address-specific information.
statements.trigger: RCPT received and address not deliverable as specified
actions: OR send 550 with no address-specific information

statements.subject: server
statements.description: if a 251 code is used, they MUST NOT assume that the client will actually update address information or even return that information to the user.
statements.guard_semantics: server MUST NOT assume client updates address after 251 reply

statements.subject: server
statements.description: if a 551 code is used, they MUST NOT assume that the client will actually update address information or even return that information to the user.
statements.guard_semantics: server MUST NOT assume client updates address after 551 reply

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a normal (i.e., 250) response is returned to VRFY, the response MAY include the full name of the user and MUST include the mailbox of the user.
actions: send 250 reply with mailbox of user

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When a name that is the argument to VRFY could identify more than one mailbox, the server MAY either note the ambiguity or identify the alternatives — 553 User ambiguous or multiline 553.
statements.trigger: VRFY command received with ambiguous argument

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a request is made to apply VRFY to a mailing list, a positive response MAY be given if a message so addressed would be delivered to everyone on the list, otherwise an error SHOULD be reported (e.g., '550 That is a mailing list, not a user' or '252 Unable to verify members of mailing list').
statements.trigger: VRFY command received with mailing list argument
actions: send 250 reply if all-delivery guaranteed, else send 550 or 252 error reply

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For the EXPN command, the string identifies a mailing list, and the successful (i.e., 250) multiline response MAY include the full name of the users and MUST give the mailboxes on the mailing list.
statements.trigger: EXPN command received with valid mailing list argument
actions: send 250 multiline reply with mailboxes on mailing list

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a request is made to expand a user name, the server MAY return a positive response consisting of a list containing one name, or an error MAY be reported (e.g., '550 That is a user name, not a mailing list').
statements.trigger: EXPN command received with user name argument
actions: send 250 single-entry reply or send 550 error reply

statements.subject: server
statements.description: C: EXPN Executive-Washroom-List / S: 550 Access Denied to You — EXPN command may result in access denied error response.
statements.trigger: EXPN command received and access denied

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When normal (2yz or 551) responses are returned from a VRFY or EXPN request, the reply MUST include the <Mailbox> name using a "<local-part@domain>" construction.
statements.trigger: VRFY or EXPN command received with normal response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Since they were both optional in RFC 821, but VRFY was made mandatory in RFC 1123, if EXPN is supported, it MUST be listed as a service extension in an EHLO response.
statements.guard_semantics: server.expn_supported = true

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For security reasons, implementations MAY provide local installations a way to disable either or both of these commands (VRFY, EXPN) through configuration options or the equivalent.
statements.trigger: VRFY or EXPN command received while command is disabled
actions: refuse or reject VRFY or EXPN command

statements.subject: server
statements.description: VRFY MAY be listed as a convenience but, since support for it is required, SMTP clients are not required to check for its presence on the extension list before using it.
actions: client may send VRFY without checking EHLO extension list

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MUST NOT return a 250 code in response to a VRFY or EXPN command unless it has actually verified the address.
statements.trigger: VRFY or EXPN command received with address actually verified

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MUST NOT return 250 if all it has done is to verify that the syntax given is valid. In that case, 502 (Command not implemented) or 500 (Syntax error, command unrecognized) SHOULD be returned.
statements.trigger: VRFY or EXPN command received with only syntax validation performed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: There may be circumstances where an address appears to be valid but cannot reasonably be verified in real time. In these situations, reply code 252 SHOULD be returned.
statements.trigger: VRFY or EXPN command received with apparent validity but real-time verification not feasible

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Reply codes 251 and 551 with VRFY (and EXPN) to indicate addresses that are recognized but that would be forwarded or rejected were mail received for them.
statements.trigger: VRFY or EXPN command received for recognized but forwardable or rejectable address

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SMTP servers MAY decline to act as mail relays or to accept addresses that specify source routes.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When route information is encountered, SMTP servers MAY ignore the route information and simply send to the final destination specified as the last element in the route and SHOULD do so.
actions: send to final destination specified as last element in route

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When source routes are not used, the reverse-path at the time of delivery will simply be the address that appeared in the MAIL command.
statements.guard_semantics: source routes not used

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If [the relay server] accepts the task, it then becomes an SMTP client, establishes a transmission channel to the next SMTP server specified in the DNS, and sends it the mail.
actions: establish transmission channel to next SMTP server
send mail to next SMTP server

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If [the relay server] declines to relay mail to a particular address for policy reasons, a 550 response SHOULD be returned.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The relay server may accept or reject the task of relaying the mail in the same way it accepts or rejects mail for a local user.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If an SMTP server has accepted the task of relaying the mail and later finds that the destination is incorrect or that the mail cannot be delivered for some other reason, then it MUST construct an 'undeliverable mail' notification message and send it to the originator of the undeliverable mail (as indicated by the reverse-path).
actions: send notification to originator at reverse-path

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When such a message is transmitted, the reverse-path MUST be set to null. A MAIL command with a null reverse-path appears as follows: MAIL FROM:<>
statements.guard_semantics: transaction.message_type = notification

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SMTP servers MUST NOT send notification messages about problems transporting notification messages. One way to prevent loops in error reporting is to specify a null reverse-path in the MAIL command of a notification message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A relay SMTP has no need to inspect or act upon the header section or body of the message data and MUST NOT do so except to add its own 'Received:' header field and, optionally, to attempt to detect looping in the mail system.
actions: do not inspect message header section or body
do not modify message header fields or text

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: An SMTP connection is terminated when the client sends a QUIT command. The server responds with a positive reply code, after which it closes the connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: An SMTP connection is terminated when the client sends a QUIT command. The server responds with a positive reply code (221), after which it closes the connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: After detecting the need to shut down the SMTP service and returning a 421 response code. This response code can be issued after the server receives any command or, if necessary, asynchronously from command receipt.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: After a timeout, as specified in Section 4.5.3.2, occurs waiting for the client to send a command or data.
statements.trigger: timeout waiting for client command or data

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers are expected to be tolerant of unknown commands, issuing a 500 reply and awaiting further instructions from the client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An SMTP server that is forcibly shut down via external means SHOULD attempt to send a line containing a 421 response code to the SMTP client before exiting.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: SMTP clients that experience a connection close, reset, or other communications failure due to circumstances not under their control SHOULD treat the mail transaction as if a 451 response had been received and act accordingly.
statements.trigger: connection close, reset, or communications failure not under client control
actions: treat mail transaction as if 451 response received

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: When a message is delivered or forwarded to each address of an expanded list form, the return address in the envelope ("MAIL FROM:") MUST be changed to be the address of a person or other entity who administers the list.
statements.guard_semantics: message is being forwarded to expanded mailing list recipients

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In the case of list forwarding, the message header section MUST be left unchanged; in particular, the "From" field of the header section is unaffected.
statements.guard_semantics: message is being forwarded to expanded mailing list recipients

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When a message is sent to a pseudo-mailbox (exploder), copies are forwarded or redistributed to each mailbox in the expanded list, with MAIL FROM changed to the list administrator and message headers left unchanged.
statements.trigger: recipient address resolves to mailing list or alias
actions: expand alias or list to individual recipient addresses
set MAIL FROM to list administrator address
forward copy of message to each expanded recipient

statements.subject: message
statements.description: To expand a list, the recipient mailer replaces the pseudo-mailbox address in the envelope with each of the expanded addresses in turn. The return (backward-pointing) address in the envelope is changed so that all error messages generated by the final deliveries will be returned to a list administrator.
actions: replace pseudo-mailbox address in envelope with each expanded address
change reverse-path (backward-pointing) address to list administrator address

statements.subject: message
statements.description: When a list constrains its processing to the very limited set of modifications and actions described here, it is attempting to emulate an MTA; such lists can be treated as a continuation in email transit.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Mailing lists that perform additional, sometimes extensive, modifications to a message and its envelope need to be viewed as full MUAs, which accept a delivery and post a new message.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The reverse-path is the argument of the MAIL command... there is a reverse-path buffer... to hold the types of data objects

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: the forward-path is the argument of the RCPT command... there is a... forward-path buffer... to hold the types of data objects

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: the mail data is the argument of the DATA command... there is a... mail data buffer... to hold the types of data objects

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: These arguments or data objects must be transmitted and held, pending the confirmation communicated by the end of mail data indication that finalizes the transaction.
statements.pre_cond: transaction.reverse_path_buffer != null & transaction.forward_path_buffer != null & transaction.mail_data_buffer != null

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Specific commands cause information to be appended to a specific buffer, or cause one or more buffers to be cleared.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Several commands (RSET, DATA, QUIT) are specified as not permitting parameters. In the absence of specific extensions offered by the server and accepted by the client, clients MUST NOT send such parameters and servers SHOULD reject commands containing them as having invalid syntax.
actions: reject command with invalid syntax response

statements.subject: session
statements.description: These commands, and a '250 OK' reply to one of them, confirm that both the SMTP client and the SMTP server are in the initial state, that is, there is no transaction in progress and all state tables and buffers are cleared.
statements.invariant_cond: transaction.in_progress = false & state_tables.cleared = true & buffers.cleared = true

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A client SMTP SHOULD start an SMTP session by issuing the EHLO command.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: These commands, and a '250 OK' reply to one of them, confirm that both the SMTP client and the SMTP server are in the initial state, that is, there is no transaction in progress and all state tables and buffers are cleared.
statements.post_cond: transaction.in_progress = false & state_tables.cleared = true & buffers.cleared = true

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A client MUST issue HELO or EHLO before starting a mail transaction.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: A client MUST issue HELO or EHLO before starting a mail transaction.
statements.guard_semantics: client.sent_EHLO = true | client.sent_HELO = true

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the SMTP server supports the SMTP service extensions, it will give a successful response, a failure response, or an error response. If the SMTP server, in violation of this specification, does not support any SMTP service extensions, it will generate an error response.
actions: send 250 successful response | send failure response | send error response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Older client SMTP systems MAY use HELO instead of EHLO, and servers MUST support the HELO command and reply properly to it.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: This command is used to initiate a mail transaction. The MAIL command may be sent only when no mail transaction is in progress. This command clears the reverse-path buffer, the forward-path buffer, and the mail data buffer, and it inserts the reverse-path information from its argument clause into the reverse-path buffer.
actions: insert reverse-path information into reverse-path buffer

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The MAIL command may be sent only when no mail transaction is in progress, see Section 4.1.4.
statements.guard_semantics: MAIL command is only valid when transaction.in_progress = false

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This command appends its forward-path argument to the forward-path buffer; it does not change the reverse-path buffer nor the mail data buffer.
statements.trigger: RCPT TO command received and accepted
actions: append forward-path argument to forward-path buffer

statements.subject: server
statements.description: xyz.com MAY also reject the message entirely when the RCPT command is received, using a 550 code (since this is a 'policy reason').
statements.trigger: RCPT TO command received with policy violation

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: This command appends its forward-path argument to the forward-path buffer; it does not change the reverse-path buffer nor the mail data buffer.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Multiple recipients are specified by multiple uses of this command.
actions: append additional forward-path to forward-path buffer

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When mail reaches its ultimate destination (the forward-path contains only a destination mailbox), the SMTP server inserts it into the destination mailbox in accordance with its host mail conventions.
actions: insert mail into destination mailbox per host mail conventions

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The receiver normally sends a 354 response to DATA, and then treats the lines following the command as mail data from the sender. This command causes the mail data to be appended to the mail data buffer.
actions: treat following lines as mail data
append mail data to mail data buffer

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Receipt of the end of mail data indication requires the server to process the stored mail transaction information. This processing consumes the information in the reverse-path buffer, the forward-path buffer, and the mail data buffer, and on the completion of this command these buffers are cleared.
statements.trigger: end of mail data indication received
statements.post_cond: reverse_path_buffer = empty & forward_path_buffer = empty & mail_data_buffer = empty

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the processing is successful, the receiver MUST send an OK reply. In sending a positive "250 OK" completion reply to the end of data indication, the receiver takes full responsibility for the message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the processing fails, the receiver MUST send a failure reply. The SMTP model does not allow for partial failures at this point: either the message is accepted by the server for delivery and a positive response is returned or it is not accepted and a failure reply is returned.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Receipt of the end of mail data indication requires the server to process the stored mail transaction information. This processing consumes the information in the reverse-path buffer, the forward-path buffer, and the mail data buffer, and on the completion of this command these buffers are cleared.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When the SMTP server accepts a message either for relaying or for final delivery, it inserts a trace record at the top of the mail data.
statements.trigger: message accepted for relaying or final delivery
actions: insert trace record at top of mail data

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: This command specifies that the current mail transaction will be aborted. Any stored sender, recipients, and mail data MUST be discarded, and all buffers and state tables cleared. The receiver MUST send a '250 OK' reply to a RSET command with no arguments. A reset command may be issued by the client at any time.
statements.post_cond: transaction.sender = null & transaction.recipients = null & transaction.mail_data = null & session.buffers_cleared = true
actions: clear all buffers and state tables

statements.subject: session
statements.description: It is effectively equivalent to a NOOP (i.e., it has no effect) if issued immediately after EHLO, before EHLO is issued in the session, after an end of data indicator has been sent and acknowledged, or immediately before a QUIT.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = <immediately after EHLO> | protocol.state = <before EHLO issued> | protocol.state = <after end of data acknowledged> | protocol.state = <immediately before QUIT>

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An SMTP server MUST NOT close the connection as the result of receiving a RSET; that action is reserved for QUIT (see Section 4.1.1.10).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SMTP servers SHOULD be prepared for this condition and SHOULD treat it as if a QUIT had been received before the connection disappeared.
statements.trigger: TCP connection closed or reset indication

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This command asks the receiver to confirm that the argument identifies a user or mailbox. This command has no effect on the reverse-path buffer, the forward-path buffer, or the mail data buffer.
statements.post_cond: session.reverse_path_buffer.unchanged = true & session.forward_path_buffer.unchanged = true & session.mail_data_buffer.unchanged = true
actions: return user or mailbox confirmation information

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: This command has no effect on the reverse-path buffer, the forward-path buffer, or the mail data buffer.
statements.guard_semantics: VRFY must not modify reverse_path_buffer, forward_path_buffer, or mail_data_buffer

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This command has no effect on the reverse-path buffer, the forward-path buffer, or the mail data buffer, and it may be issued at any time.
statements.post_cond: reverse_path_buffer.unchanged = true & forward_path_buffer.unchanged = true & mail_data_buffer.unchanged = true
actions: confirm argument identifies a mailing list
return mailing list membership in multi-line reply

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the command is successful, a reply is returned containing information as described in Section 3.5.
actions: send success reply with mailing list membership

statements.subject: session
statements.description: This command has no effect on the reverse-path buffer, the forward-path buffer, or the mail data buffer, and it may be issued at any time.
statements.guard_semantics: EXPN does not modify reverse_path_buffer, forward_path_buffer, or mail_data_buffer; valid in any session state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: This command has no effect on the reverse-path buffer, the forward-path buffer, or the mail data buffer, and it may be issued at any time.
statements.post_cond: session.state = session.state & session.reverse_path_buffer = session.reverse_path_buffer & session.forward_path_buffer = session.forward_path_buffer & session.mail_data_buffer = session.mail_data_buffer

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SMTP servers SHOULD support HELP without arguments and MAY support it with arguments.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: NOOP specifies no action other than that the receiver send a '250 OK' reply. It has no effect on the reverse-path buffer, the forward-path buffer, or the mail data buffer, and it may be issued at any time.
statements.post_cond: session.reverse_path_buffer = session.reverse_path_buffer & session.forward_path_buffer = session.forward_path_buffer & session.mail_data_buffer = session.mail_data_buffer

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If a parameter string is specified, servers SHOULD ignore it.
statements.guard_semantics: ignored by server if present

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This command specifies that the receiver MUST send a '221 OK' reply, and then close the transmission channel.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The sender MUST NOT intentionally close the transmission channel until it sends a QUIT command, and it SHOULD wait until it receives the reply (even if there was an error response to a previous command).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the connection is closed prematurely due to violations of the above or system or network failure, the server MUST cancel any pending transaction, but not undo any previously completed transaction, and generally MUST act as if the command or transaction in progress had received a temporary error (i.e., a 4yz response).
actions: treat in-progress command or transaction as 4yz temporary error

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The QUIT command may be issued at any time. Any current uncompleted mail transaction will be aborted.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The receiver MUST send a '221 OK' reply, and then close the transmission channel. (Terminal state reached after QUIT is processed.)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The receiver MUST NOT intentionally close the transmission channel until it receives and replies to a QUIT command (even if there was an error).
statements.guard_semantics: server may not close transmission channel unless session.quit_received = true

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server SMTP does not recognize or cannot implement one or more of the parameters associated with a particular MAIL FROM or RCPT TO command, it will return code 555.
statements.trigger: MAIL FROM or RCPT TO received with unrecognized or unimplementable parameters

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If, for some reason, the server is temporarily unable to accommodate one or more of the parameters associated with a MAIL FROM or RCPT TO command, and if the definition of the specific parameter does not mandate the use of another code, it should return code 455.
statements.trigger: MAIL FROM or RCPT TO received with temporarily unavailable parameters

statements.subject: server

actions: reset state as if RSET issued

statements.description: When mail is rejected for policy reasons (e.g., relay filtering), a 550 code SHOULD be used in response to EHLO (or HELO) as appropriate.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When mail is rejected for policy reasons (e.g., relay filtering), a 550 code SHOULD be used in response to MAIL as appropriate.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When mail is rejected for policy reasons (e.g., relay filtering), a 550 code SHOULD be used in response to RCPT as appropriate.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Implementations SHOULD provide the capability to perform relay filtering (limiting relay function to known or identifiable sources).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server that is reached by means of a source route (e.g., its domain name appears first in the list in the forward-path) MUST remove its domain name from any forward-paths in which that domain name appears before forwarding the message and MAY remove all other source routing information.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The reverse-path SHOULD NOT be updated by servers conforming to this specification.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SMTP servers MUST NOT derive final message routing information from message header fields.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: clients SHOULD NOT transmit source routes

statements.subject: server
statements.description: servers MUST be prepared to receive and handle them as discussed in Section 3.3 and Appendix F.2

statements.subject: server
statements.description: S: 220 foo.com Simple Mail Transfer Service Ready — server sends 220 greeting upon connection open

statements.subject: session
statements.description: C: EHLO bar.com / S: 250-foo.com greets bar.com / S: 250 HELP — client sends EHLO, server responds with 250 multi-line capability list

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: C: MAIL FROM:<Smith@bar.com> / S: 250 OK — client initiates mail transaction, server accepts with 250

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: C: RCPT TO:<Jones@foo.com> / S: 250 OK — server accepts recipient with 250

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: C: RCPT TO:<Green@foo.com> / S: 550 No such user here — server rejects recipient with 550; transaction continues for other recipients

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: C: DATA / S: 354 Start mail input; end with <CRLF>.<CRLF> — client sends DATA command, server responds 354 and enters data-input state

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: C: . / S: 250 OK — client sends end-of-data indicator (<CRLF>.<CRLF>), server accepts message with 250

statements.subject: session
statements.description: C: QUIT / S: 221 foo.com Service closing transmission channel — client sends QUIT, server closes with 221

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: C: RSET / S: 250 OK — in aborted scenario, client sends RSET after partial RCPT sequence; server acknowledges and resets transaction state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: C: VRFY Crispin / S: 250 Mark Crispin <Admin.MRC@foo.com> — client issues VRFY before MAIL FROM; server responds 250 with verified address; session remains in pre-transaction state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: D.3 Relayed Mail Scenario Step 1: source host fails connection to primary MX (xyz.com) and opens connection to relay (foo.com); relay accepts message. Step 2: relay then opens new connection to xyz.com and forwards the message — illustrating that each relay hop is a distinct SMTP session
statements.trigger: relay connection established to next-hop server
actions: open new SMTP session to next-hop
forward message with updated Received header
